title: UTI Symptoms Triage Protocol
body: UTI assessment: Determine symptoms — dysuria (burning with urination), frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, hematuria, and urine changes (cloudy, foul-smelling). Ask about associated symptoms: fever, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, rigors (suggest upper tract / pyelonephritis). Ask about pregnancy status, diabetes, immunosuppression, recurrent UTI history, recent catheterization. In males, UTI is less common and may need broader workup. Red flags: high fever with flank pain (pyelonephritis), rigors, inability to keep fluids down, pregnant with UTI symptoms, urinary retention.
disposition_notes: Fever with flank pain or rigors → URGENT_CARE or ER_NOW if sepsis suspected. Pregnant with UTI symptoms → URGENT_CARE. Uncomplicated lower UTI symptoms in non-pregnant female → SAME_DAY. Mild recurrent symptoms in known UTI-prone patient → ROUTINE or SAME_DAY.
